text:
The Devils lost 3-2 to Montreal on Wednesday, Connor Hellebuyck's first defeat as their starter after a 7-0 run, and it barely dents the picture. New Jersey is 15-7-0 with 30 points, and unlike most hot starts, this one is backed by the chances.

The Devils have 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 56% at five on five. Their record sits right where their play says it should, with no luck to give back. The penalty kill allows just 0.48 expected goals a game, and they take only 2.77 penalties a game while drawing 3.77, which keeps them out of trouble and on the power play. Our playoff odds are 95%.

The lines both work. Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored teams 12-7 with 61% of the chances; Nico Hischier, who just reached 500 career points, does the same with Timo Meier and Luke Evangelista. On the back end, Luke Hughes has been the story, with The New York Times writing about his breakout, and his pair with Brett Pesce has outscored opponents 20-9 in 326 minutes.

Hellebuyck arrived after forcing his way out of Winnipeg, and a strong team got a goalie it didn't strictly need. Watch the five-on-five share against good teams; the Habs, per Fink, gave them things to address.
headline: The Devils are as good as their record
